To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ability to learn complex relations is a general cognitive capacity that is not dependent on conscious awareness; (2) learning complex relations is not dependent on the ability to learn a sequence of pairs; (3) the ability to perform a transitive inference task is dependent on learning a hierarchy, but not necessarily learning a sequence of pairs.

(1) participants who were not aware of the task structure (uninformed participants) performed at a high level on a transitive inference task; (2) uninformed participants' performance did not correlate with postexperimental measures of awareness; and (3) performance on the transitivity task did not correlate with measures of awareness.
Relational learning with nonverbal stimuli can occur without conscious awareness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of conscious processes in learning.
the nature of learning and the role of consciousness in learning.
the question of whether conscious awareness of the task is a necessary condition for successful relational learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
relational learning is not a conscious process.
the conscious and unconscious processes involved in relational learning tasks are not necessarily identical.
relational learning tasks are not necessarily dependent upon conscious processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
conscious processes are not essential for relational learning, but that they may be important for the flexibility that is required for relational learning.
conscious awareness is not necessary for learning and memory.
the ability to represent and learn relationships between stimuli is not a conscious function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to flexibly encode and retrieve information is not necessarily a conscious process.
relational learning tasks are not necessarily conscious processes.
relational learning is not always accompanied by explicit knowledge of the structure of the learning environment.
